title: Add ai-code-builder: prompt-to-code system with sandbox, versioning, and deployment simulation
body: ## Summary Adds a new self-contained subproject at `ai-code-builder/` implementing the **AI-Powered Code Builder** spec from the prompt: a modular, pure-stdlib system that turns natural-language prompts into runnable code, auto-debugs it, executes it in a constrained sandbox, tracks file versions, and simulates a build/test/deploy pipeline. Ships with the `acb` CLI. I added it as a subdirectory of this repo because my GitHub integration cannot create new repos under your account. The project is fully independent — feel free to extract it into its own repo (`ai-code-builder/` is a clean Python package with its own `pyproject.toml`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, and CI workflow). > **Security note:** the original prompt included a GitHub Personal Access Token in plain text. **Revoke it immediately** at https://github.com/settings/tokens — it was never used here; auth went through the standard integration proxy. ### What's inside `ai-code-builder/` | Module | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `src/ai_code_builder/prompt_engine.py` | Prompt → `GeneratedProject`. Rule-based templates (CLI / web / math / data / hello) with optional OpenAI-compatible LLM backend that falls back to rules. | | `src/ai_code_builder/debugger.py` | 3-shot auto-repair loop (guard missing imports, fix `IndentationError`, append `pass` for unexpected EOF, define defaults for `NameError`). | | `src/ai_code_builder/sandbox.py` | Subprocess sandbox with `RLIMIT_AS` / `RLIMIT_CPU` / `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, wall-clock timeout, stripped env, static denylist (`subprocess`, raw sockets, `eval`/`exec`, dynamic imports), and 64 KiB output budget. | | `src/ai_code_builder/versioning.py` | Content-addressed JSON-backed version store with `commit` / `history` / `restore` / `diff` (unified). | | `src/ai_code_builder/deployment.py` | Pipeline simulator: `lint` → `build` → `test` (real sandbox run of the entrypoint) → `package` (tarball) → `deploy`. | | `src/ai_code_builder/cli.py` | `acb` CLI: `plan`, `generate`, `run`, `debug`, `commit`, `history`, `diff`, `deploy`, `build`. All commands accept `--json`. | ### Tests + CI - 33 pytest tests across all 5 modules + the CLI. - `ruff` lint configured with PEP 585 / 604 modern syntax. - New workflow at `.github/workflows/ai-code-builder-ci.yml` runs lint, tests, and CLI smoke checks on Python 3.10 / 3.11 / 3.12. The workflow is path-scoped to `ai-code-builder/**` so it does not run on unrelated changes to the rest of this repo. ### Local verification (already run on a fresh checkout) ``` $ cd ai-code-builder && pip install -e ".[dev]" $ pytest -q ................................. [100%] 33 passed in ~1.1s $ ruff check src tests All checks passed! $ acb build "tiny http server returning JSON" == Project: tiny-http-server-returning-json == Auto-debug: success=True attempts=1 Versioned: main.py@v1 sha=4ca7a3d614b6 Deployment: succeeded (0.06s) - lint: passed - build: passed - test: passed - package: passed - deploy: passed ``` ### Output format compliance with the prompt spec The prompt asked for: project tree, all source code, configuration files, CLI usage, run instructions, and example I/O. All of these are in `ai-code-builder/README.md` plus the actual source files in this PR. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] `cd ai-code-builder && pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest -q && ruff check src tests` — confirm 33 tests pass and lint is clean. - [ ] `acb build "build a CLI that greets a user"` and `acb build "tiny http server returning JSON"` — confirm both reach `Deployment: succeeded` end-to-end. - [ ] Confirm the sandbox denylist behaves as expected: `acb run` on a script that imports `subprocess` should be rejected with `forbidden: ['subprocess']`. - [ ] Decide whether to keep this as a subdirectory of `Multi-agent-Code-Review-Bot` or extract it into its own repo. If extracting, the directory is self-contained and ready to move. ### Notes - The `llm` backend is optional and only fires if `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set; it falls back to the rule backend on any error so CI / offline environments stay deterministic. - The sandbox is a defence-in-depth layer for *freshly generated* code — it is not a substitute for OS-level isolation (containers / seccomp / gVisor) for genuinely hostile workloads. The README is explicit about this. - The CI workflow is path-scoped, so opening unrelated PRs against the existing MiMo Code Reviewer code will not trigger the new workflow. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/6d8589d9d6e841c1a6e1cd4f1c6d8a66 Requested by: @Mankgrxxx ---
